title: Higher-dimensional chaotic features and random matrix signatures following a local quench
abstract: We study the multidimensional erratic structure of correlation functions produced by local operator quenches in finite-volume free massive scalar field theory in dimensions 2 and 3. The basic observable is the subtracted equal-time two-point function in the locally excited state and its spatiotemporal patterns of extrema. We analyze these extrema by the multidimensional diagnostics recently introduced for chaotic scattering amplitudes and related problems: all-pair distance distributions, nearest-neighbor spacings, greedy-path spacing ratios, and the extrema form factor. For the $1+1$-dimensional local quench we find that, in the regime of small Euclidean smearing, the fitted extremum statistics move close to the $β=1$ random-matrix benchmark, while increasing the smearing scale softens the effective repulsion and moves the distributions away from the GOE-like value. For the $2+1$-dimensional local quench we find that the nearest-neighbor statistics of the refined extrema are close to, or above, the $β=1$ benchmark, and the greedy-path ratio statistics are described by even larger effective $β$ values. Finally we studied the all-pair extrema spatial form factor and found that, in the one-, two-, and three-dimensional cases, its main structure is controlled by the corresponding uniform interval, rectangle, or cuboid geometry of the extrema cloud and found the dip-ram-plateau structure in the last two cases. Thus the form factor provides a complementary global diagnostic of how the extrema fill their effective metric support, while the genuinely nontrivial local and mesoscopic organization is carried by the nearest-neighbor and greedy-path statistics.
summary: This paper analyzes the statistical patterns of extrema found in two-point correlation functions following a local quench in free scalar field theories. By applying advanced point process diagnostics, the authors test whether these chaotic features adhere to standard random matrix theory predictions or reveal deeper geometric organization dictated by the dimensionality of the system.
main_problem: The study investigates the multidimensional erratic structure of correlation functions generated by local operator quenches in quantum field theory.
main_result: Extremum statistics show behavior approaching $\beta=1$ random-matrix benchmarks in 1+1 dimensions, while higher dimensions reveal geometry-controlled features via the all-pair extremum spatial form factor.
method: The analysis employs advanced statistical diagnostics—including all-pair distance distributions, nearest-neighbor spacings, and greedy-path ratios—applied to the point cloud formed by the extrema of the two-point correlation function.
model_or_system: The system is a free massive scalar field theory undergoing a local operator quench in finite volume (analyzed first in 1+1D, then generalized to 2+1D). The observable is the subtracted equal-time two-point function.
key_observables: Extrema of the correlation function; All-pair distance distribution; Nearest-neighbor spacing statistics; Greedy-path ratio statistics; All-pair extremum spatial form factor (ExFF).
important_parameters: Euclidean smearing scale ($\alpha$); Dimensionality (1D vs 2D space); Comparison benchmarks ($\beta=1$, GOE).
main_assumptions: The analysis treats the extrema as a point process whose statistics can be mapped onto known random matrix ensembles or geometric laws.
figures_summary: Not specified, but diagnostics are compared against theoretical curves for uniform intervals, rectangles, and cuboids in the form factor analysis.
paper_structure: The paper systematically defines the physical model (local quench), introduces the statistical framework using multiple point-process diagnostics, analyzes results sequentially from 1+1D to 2+1D, and concludes by interpreting the role of geometry versus universal RMT laws.
why_interesting: It applies sophisticated tools from quantum chaos and random matrix theory—typically used for energy spectra—to analyze non-equilibrium correlation functions in condensed matter systems, providing a new diagnostic tool for quench dynamics.
